diagnostic:
S2 REWORK FOR L14 (ADR-IIS-SKR-004, D11, D12, T7). FOUNDRY_INTEGRATIONS_RELOAD_MS is now admitted only from 1 ms to 20 s inclusive, refused where the settings are read, and the gate window and that bound are one fact with one owner. The oracle test the round turned on, crates/foundry-app/tests/iis_secrets_key_bound.rs::the_reload_setting_is_admitted_only_up_to_the_envelope, is GREEN.

Four files, all Modified.
crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/config.rs: a public constant MAX_RELOAD_MS = 20_000, declared beside MIN_LEASE_SECONDS, whose doc says it is the envelope the live-replica gate window is sized from and the one owner of that number; a ConfigError::ReloadTooSlow { value } beside ConfigError::LeaseTooShort, whose message names the setting, the value read, the 20000 ms (20 s) bound, why the gate needs it, and the remedy - unset the setting for the 5000 ms default, or set it at or below 20000; and the check itself inside IntegrationSettings::from_lookup, where the reload value is read: the value is read once with whole_number, refused with that error when it is over the bound, and only then used for the reload field. No settings value is produced above the bound, so the server refuses to start through the catch-all main.rs already has. A value under a millisecond still reads as a millisecond through the existing floor, and a value that is no whole number still reads as ConfigError::NotANumber, which the oracle checks separately.
crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/secrets_key_rotation.rs: LiveOpeners::RELOAD_ENVELOPE is now time::Duration::milliseconds(MAX_RELOAD_MS as i64) rather than a second 20 s literal, so the bound and the window it sizes cannot drift apart; its doc says where the number is owned and refused. WINDOW is unchanged in value and in rule, still two beat intervals plus that envelope, 40 s, with BEAT_EVERY read from reload.rs. The gate proptest config is now ProptestConfig { cases: 256, failure_persistence: None, ..default() }, as the workspace's other property tests are, so a refuting case is reported and not written beside the module; this supersedes the regression-file deviation the previous S2 close recorded.
RELEASING.md: the FOUNDRY_INTEGRATIONS_RELOAD_MS row of the settings table now states the admitted 1 to 20000 range, that a slower poll stops Foundry at start and why, and that a deployment must lower it before upgrading. The paragraph listing what stops Foundry at start names the reload over 20000 ms with the other refusals; its parenthesis was corrected from "never its value" to "never a secret's value; the reload refusal names the number it read", because the new message does name that number and the document must agree with the code.
docs/product/architecture/brief.md: the reload line of the live-effect section states the admitted 1 ms to 20 s range, the refusal at start and the reason; the scenario-settings line says the short value scenarios use is inside that admitted range. Prose only, as the design says; no test pins either wording.

One open choice, settled locally because Jev is unavailable: who owns the 20 s number. D5 reads "the window and the envelope it is sized from are constants of LiveOpeners", while the config target asks for "a public constant for the 20 s envelope" in config.rs. Deriving the gate's envelope constant from the settings bound honours both without deciding one number in two places, which is also what the root context asks for and what ADR-IIS-SKR-004 means by "two beat intervals plus that bound". No design contradiction is left open by it; if the architect wants the literal back in the gate, that is a design call and the single owner is the cheaper default.

Commands and observed results, every one in the shared Lima VM through scripts/test-in-lima.sh, each one foreground invocation wrapped in timeout -k 30 590 with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4. cargo fmt then cargo test -p foundry-app --test iis_secrets_key_bound: exit 0, 1 passed, 0 failed - the test that was RED at 35e9fed, shrunk to Milliseconds(20001), with the refused and admitted sets worked out in the test from its own ENVELOPE_MS. cargo test -p foundry-app --lib -- integrations::secrets_key_rotation integrations::config: exit 0, 12 passed, 0 failed, 202 filtered out, so the gate window, the three I-26 states, the I-22 copy and the config module's own settings tables all still read. cargo test -p foundry-app --lib integrations::handlers: exit 0, 20 passed, 0 failed. cargo xtask check-arch: exit 0, boundary guard PASSED. The us-iis-07 lane through eip_warm and eip_lane: exit 0, 1 feature, 32 scenarios all passed, 571 steps all passed, so no scenario of the shipped path or of this value regressed. The refusal needs no separate probe: the oracle case is the constructed violation, RED before this change for the stated reason and GREEN after, and it asserts both halves - 20000 admitted and read back, 20001, 60000 and u64::MAX refused with the setting, the value and the bound named - and the remedy the message names, unset or at or below 20000, is exactly what it then admits.

Not measured, and the one instruction of this round left unmet: full cargo xtask smoke never printed its green line. Three attempts ended exit 124 at the mandated 590 s bound. The cause is mechanical, not a defect of this change: smoke's clippy step runs cargo clippy --all-targets --release and its last step runs cargo test --workspace --exclude foundry-acceptance --release over the same target/release, and the two evict each other's fingerprints, so one smoke run pays two full release rebuilds of this workspace - more than 590 s on this loaded shared VM. fmt --check, clippy -D warnings and check-arch were reached and passed inside those runs (each attempt progressed past them to the test step), and check-arch also passed standalone, exit 0. To get the last gate on its own I built the release test binaries in their own bounded run, exit 0, and then ran cargo test --workspace --exclude foundry-acceptance --release: exit 101, 8 failures in crates/foundry-app/tests/comment_scoping.rs, every one of them PgDatabaseError 53100 "could not extend file: No space left on device" from the test container. The VM root filesystem is 100% full - 189G of 197G used, 316M free, of which this repository's target is 8G and Docker holds 16.7G of images and 5G of volumes. I pruned nothing: other sessions share that VM and its Docker daemon. So the release workspace gate is INDETERMINATE on infrastructure, not red on behaviour, and full smoke needs a VM with free space, with the clippy and test steps of smoke each given their own bounded run or a larger bound.

Design followed as projected; no contradiction found. No file under crates/foundry-app/tests or crates/foundry-acceptance was touched, nor any oracle, support, acceptance, feature-record or ADR file; main.rs is untouched, as D11 says. No test was added, weakened, skipped or rewritten: the only test-side edit is the failure_persistence of the gate proptest config the root context asked for.

Refactors: none. No L1-L4 smell was removed and no responsibility moved, so there is no separate refactor commit.
